root_cause.text: The error handling in `airoha_qdma_rx_process()` conditionally released page_pool fragments only when no skb had been allocated, causing a memory leak when an error occurred on a subsequent buffer after the skb was partially built, because the fragment was never linked to the skb and the else branch was skipped.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the `else` condition so that `page_pool_put_full_page()` is always called after freeing the skb in the error path, and the commit description states: "If an error occurs on the subsequents buffers belonging to the non-linear part of the skb ... the page_pool fragment will not be linked to the skb so it will not return to the pool in the airoha_qdma_rx_process() error path."

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch removes the `else` condition so that `page_pool_put_full_page()` is always called after freeing the skb in the error path, and the commit description states: "If an error occurs on the subsequents buffers belonging to the non-linear part of the skb ... the page_pool fragment will not be linked to the skb so it will not return to the pool in the airoha_qdma_rx_process() error path."

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix page leak by always returning the page to the page pool after RX processing, regardless of whether an skb is attached.
intent_record.what: Removed the else branch from an if-else block, making page_pool_put_full_page() call unconditional after handling the skb.
intent_record.how: Previously, the page was only returned to the page pool when q->skb was NULL. Now, the page is always returned to the page pool after RX packet processing, even when an skb was freed.

grouping_result.intent: Fix page leak by always returning the page to the page pool after RX processing, regardless of whether an skb is attached.

relevance_review.reason: The group's fix directly addresses the memory leak by ensuring page pool fragments are always returned, regardless of skb attachment, which is the exact root cause described.

candidates.rationale: This conditional causes the code to skip releasing the page pool fragment when an skb has been allocated but the fragment is not yet linked to it, leading to a memory leak on error.

vuln_statements.explanation: This conditional causes the page pool fragment release to occur only when no skb has been allocated, skipping release when an skb exists but the fragment is not yet linked, leading to a memory leak on error.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit d6d2b0e1538d5c381ec0ca95afaf772c096ea5dc
Author: Lorenzo Bianconi <lorenzo@kernel.org>
Date:   Thu May 15 08:33:06 2025 +0200

    net: airoha: Fix page recycling in airoha_qdma_rx_process()
    
    Do not recycle the page twice in airoha_qdma_rx_process routine in case
    of error. Just run dev_kfree_skb() if the skb has been allocated and marked
    for recycling. Run page_pool_put_full_page() directly if the skb has not
    been allocated yet.
    Moreover, rely on DMA address from q
bic_trace_step.reason: The diff for commit d6d2b0e1538d shows the complete change to the free_frag label in airoha_qdma_rx_process(). The new code conditionally handles the case where an skb is already allocated (dev_kfree_skb) vs. not (page_pool_put_full_page), which directly fixes the memory leak vulnerability described. The function in this commit no longer contains the vulnerable unconditional page recycling and skb freeing, so the fix is present.
